title: Product with the invertible interval projects by a categorical equivalence
statement: Use small simplicial sets, degreewise products, nerves and quasicategories from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and categorical equivalences in the test-functor convention of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $\mathcal I$ be the ordinary groupoid with objects $0,1$ and exactly one morphism between each ordered pair, and put $I=N(\mathcal I)$. For every small simplicial set $R$, the projection $\pi_R:R\times I\to R$ is a categorical equivalence. No quasicategory, nonemptiness or finiteness hypothesis on $R$ is required; the assertion holds in every input universe.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4, printed p.92: categorical equivalences are preserved by products; the contractible groupoid interval supplies the other factor. Agent-extracted auxiliary assertion from the original proof step 3 of lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison, within Proposition 4.2.1.5. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.
